items.title: pforret/mkdox2
items.text: Convenient bash wrapper for Mkdocs Material projects via Docker

items.title: 🔥 Usage
items.text:
Program : mkdox2  by peter@forret.com
Version : v2.1.2 (Nov  1 16:07:13 2026)
Purpose : easy wrapper for Zensical/Material in Docker mode
Usage   : mkdox2 [-h] [-q] [-v] [-f] [-B <TEMPLATE>] [-G] [-I] [-Q] [-R] [-T] [-X] [-l <log_dir>] [-t <tmp_dir>] [-D <DOCKER>] [-E <TITLE>] [-H <HISTORY>] [-L <LENGTH>] [-P <PORT>] [-S <SECS>] <action> <input?> <output?>
Flags, options and parameters:
    -h|--help        : [flag] show usage [default: off]
    -q|--quiet       : [flag] no output [default: off]
    -v|--verbose     : [flag] also show debug messages [default: off]
    -f|--force       : [flag] do not ask for confirmation (always yes) [default: off]
    -B|--TEMPLATE <?>: [option] template to use for mkdox new
    -G|--GITPUSH     : [flag] push to git after commit [default: off]
    -I|--INDEX       : [flag] build index.md if index.pre/.post present (for mkdox build) [default: off]
    -Q|--SHORT       : [flag] include short contents of page (for mkdox toc) [default: off]
    -R|--RECURSIVE   : [flag] also list subfolders (for mkdox toc) [default: off]
    -T|--TREE        : [flag] list as tree (for mkdox toc) [default: off]
    -X|--EXPORT      : [flag] export to PDF (for mkdox build) [default: off]
    -l|--log_dir <?> : [option] folder for log files   [default: /Users/pforret/log/mkdox2]
    -t|--tmp_dir <?> : [option] folder for temp files  [default: /tmp/mkdox2]
    -D|--DOCKER <?>  : [option] docker image to use  [default: pforret/mkdox-zensical]
    -E|--TITLE <?>   : [option] set site title
    -H|--HISTORY <?> : [option] days to take into account for mkdox recent  [default: 7]
    -L|--LENGTH <?>  : [option] max commit message length  [default: 99]
    -P|--PORT <?>    : [option] http port for serve
    -S|--SECS <?>    : [option] seconds to wait for launching a browser  [default: 5]
    <action>         : [choice] action to perform  [options: new,serve,post,blog,images,build,recent,toc,check,env,update]
    <input>          : [parameter] input folder name (optional)
    <output>         : [parameter] output file name (optional)
                                  @github.com:pforret/mkdox2.git                                             
### TIPS & EXAMPLES
* use mkdox2 new to create new Zensical project
  mkdox2 new <name>
* use mkdox2 build to create static HTML site in _site folder
  mkdox2 build
* use mkdox2 serve to start local website server (for preview)
  mkdox2 serve
* use mkdox2 images to list all images in a folder into a .md file
  mkdox2 images docs/some/folder docs/some/folder/images.md
* use mkdox2 blog to generate blog index from posts in docs/blog/posts/
  mkdox2 blog
* use mkdox2 toc <folder> <file> to create Table Of Contents for all Markdown files in folder
  mkdox2 toc faq/services
  mkdox2 -R toc . index
* use mkdox2 recent to quickly list all pages changed in last N days
  mkdox2 recent >> changes.md
  mkdox2 -H 2 recent | sed 's|* |\• |' >> changes.md
* use mkdox2 check to check if this script is ready to execute and what values the options/flags are
  mkdox2 check
* use mkdox2 env to generate an example .env file
  mkdox2 env > .env
* use mkdox2 update to update to the latest version
  mkdox2 update
* >>> bash script created with pforret/bashew
* >>> for bash development, also check out pforret/setver and pforret/progressbar

items.title: Request
items.text: default template should be: simple site, then site + blog, then Karpathy wiki and that's it
path: Limit template menu to simple, blog, Karpathy wiki

items.title: Analysis
items.text:
When mkdox2 new runs without -B/--TEMPLATE, mkdox2.sh:96-119 lists every folder under templates/*/ in glob (alphabetical) order and asks the user to pick a number. With six template folders the menu is currently: 1) ai_employee 2) committee 3) dev_project 4) karpathy_wiki 5) simple 6) with_blog. The request is a fixed, curated menu: 1) simple, 2) with_blog, 3) karpathy_wiki, and nothing else. This changes existing behaviour (the menu order and its contents), so it's a change.

Open questions: - What happens to ai_employee, committee and dev_project? Options: still reachable with -B <name> but hidden from the menu; or removed from templates/ entirely. - "Default template": should an empty answer at the prompt (just Enter) pick simple? Right now an empty answer dies with "Invalid choice". - Where the curated order lives: a hardcoded list in mkdox2.sh, or something in the template folders (e.g. an order/hidden marker next to description.txt) so adding a template needs no code change.
path: Limit template menu to simple, blog, Karpathy wiki

items.title: Impacted files
items.text:
• mkdox2.sh: the template menu loop (lines 96-119): fixed order, limited list, optional default on Enter
  • CLAUDE.md: "Template system" line only mentions simple and with_blog; add karpathy_wiki and the menu rule
  • templates/ai_employee/, templates/committee/, templates/dev_project/: only if they are removed rather than hidden
path: Limit template menu to simple, blog, Karpathy wiki

items.title: Plan
items.text:
1. Decide hide vs remove for the other three templates, and whether Enter defaults to simple.
  2. Replace the glob loop with a list in the fixed order simple with_blog karpathy_wiki, keeping the description.txt line next to each name.
  3. If chosen, accept an empty answer as choice 1 (simple) and show [1-3, Enter=1] in the prompt.
  4. Keep -B <name> validation against the folder on disk (line 120) so hidden templates still work, if kept.
  5. Update CLAUDE.md.
path: Limit template menu to simple, blog, Karpathy wiki

items.text:

  • Picking 1/2/3 creates the project from that template
  • (if chosen) pressing Enter creates a simple project
  • (if kept) mkdox2 -B dev_project new demo still works
  • shellcheck mkdox2.sh shows no new warnings; ./tests/run_tests.sh passes

items.title: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Request
items.text: update Zensical Docker image to latest version
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Analysis
items.text:
The image pforret/mkdox-zensical (default for -D/--DOCKER in mkdox2.sh:49) is built from docker/Dockerfile, which starts FROM zensical/zensical:latest and adds third-party plugins (autolinks, awesome-pages, include-markdown, rss, markdown-include). Because the base is unpinned, "updating" mostly means rebuilding with a fresh pull of the base and pushing again; push_docker.sh builds without --pull, so a stale local zensical/zensical:latest can be reused.

Risks / open questions: - Should the base be pinned to an explicit Zensical version (e.g. zensical/zensical:<x.y.z>) for reproducible builds, instead of :latest? - push_docker.sh only pushes :latest; CLAUDE.md says the image shares VERSION.md (2.1.2), but no version tag is pushed. Consider also tagging pforret/mkdox-zensical:<VERSION>. - New Zensical releases may change CLI flags (serve --dev-addr) or plugin compatibility; verify serve and build still work. - Build is linux/amd64 only; arm64 (Apple Silicon) users run under emulation. - Pushing to Docker Hub is outward-facing and needs credentials.
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Impacted files
items.text:

  • mkdox2.sh: drop --platform linux/amd64 from the 3 docker run calls (lines 82, 235, 296)
  • CLAUDE.md: Docker image section (versioning/tagging is the Zensical version, multi-arch)
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Plan
items.text: See the PRP below (pin 0.0.74, tag :latest + :0.0.74, multi-arch amd64+arm64).
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Acceptance criteria
items.text:
• docker/Dockerfile starts FROM zensical/zensical:0.0.74
  • docker run --rm --entrypoint zensical pforret/mkdox-zensical --version prints 0.0.74
  • Docker Hub has pforret/mkdox-zensical:latest and :0.0.74, each a manifest list with linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
  • mkdox2.sh has no --platform flags; new, build and serve work natively on arm64 (no platform warning)
  • shellcheck mkdox2.sh docker/push_docker.sh and ./tests/run_tests.sh pass
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: PRP
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Goal
items.text: pforret/mkdox-zensical is rebuilt on Zensical 0.0.74 (pinned, was 0.0.24 via an unpinned :latest), published as a multi-arch image (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) under both :latest and :0.0.74, and mkdox2.sh no longer forces amd64 emulation, so mkdox new|build|serve run natively on Apple Silicon.
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Why
items.text:
• The pushed image dates from 2026-02-28 and runs Zensical 0.0.24; 50 releases behind.
  • :latest base made builds non-reproducible and hid which Zensical a user runs; a version tag lets users pin with -D pforret/mkdox-zensical:0.0.74.
  • On arm64 Macs every docker run was emulated (slow serve/hot-reload, platform warnings).
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Decisions taken
items.text:
• Base image reference → pin FROM zensical/zensical:0.0.74 (user)
  • Image tags pushed → :latest + :<zensical version> (e.g. :0.0.74), not the repo VERSION.md (user) (recorded: decisions/2026-11-01.tag-pforret-mkdox-zensical-with-latest.md)
  • Architectures → multi-arch now: linux/amd64 + linux/arm64, and remove --platform linux/amd64 from mkdox2.sh (user)
  • Source of the version tag in push_docker.sh → parsed from the FROM line of the Dockerfile, so the version lives in one place (default)
  • mkdox2.sh default -D image → stays pforret/mkdox-zensical (implicit :latest) (default)
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Context the implementer MUST read
items.text:
- file: docker/Dockerfile
  why: base image + pip plugin layer; ENTRYPOINT uses /sbin/tini from the base, keep it
- file: docker/push_docker.sh
  why: current build/push; build context is "." so it must be run from docker/ — make it cd to its own dir
- file: mkdox2.sh
  why: lines 82 (new), 235 (build), 296 (serve) pass --platform linux/amd64; line 49 is the -D default
- file: CLAUDE.md
  why: "Docker image" section claims the image shares VERSION.md — update to the new tagging
- url: https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases
  section: releases 0.0.25 … 0.0.74
  critical: scan for renamed CLI flags (serve --dev-addr, build --config-file, new) and config changes before testing
- url: https://hub.docker.com/r/zensical/zensical/tags
  section: tag 0.0.74
  critical: base is published for amd64 and arm64 (verified with docker manifest inspect)
- url: https://docs.docker.com/build/building/multi-platform/
  section: "Build multi-platform images"
  critical: the local daemon uses the overlay store, not containerd, so a multi-platform build cannot --load; it must --push directly
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Known gotchas & guardrails
items.text:
• Mirror the existing patterns named under Context; do not introduce new ones for this item
  • CRITICAL: multi-platform docker buildx build here can only --push, not --load; for local testing build one platform with --platform linux/arm64 --load (host is arm64) and test that before pushing
  • CRITICAL: pass --pull so the pinned base is fetched fresh, not taken from cache
  • The pip plugins (autolinks, awesome-pages, include-markdown, rss, markdown-include) must install on arm64 too; a failure there blocks the multi-arch push
  • PRESERVE: ENTRYPOINT/CMD, WORKDIR /docs, EXPOSE 8000; mkdox2.sh calls the image as … "$DOCKER" new|build|serve …
  • PRESERVE: the --user "$(id -u)":"$(id -g)" on new and all other docker run args; only remove --platform linux/amd64
  • Users who already have the old amd64 :latest cached keep it until docker pull pforret/mkdox-zensical; mention this in CHANGELOG.md
  • Pushing to Docker Hub is outward-facing: needs docker login as pforret; confirm with the user before running the push
  • Also update: CLAUDE.md Docker image section; CHANGELOG.md entry
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Approach
items.text: Modify only existing files. docker/Dockerfile: pin the FROM tag. docker/push_docker.sh: cd to the script's directory, read the Zensical version from the Dockerfile's FROM line, then run one docker buildx build --pull --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t "$image:latest" -t "$image:$version" --push ., with set -euo pipefail. mkdox2.sh: drop --platform linux/amd64 from the three docker run calls. Order matters only here: test a single-arch local build before pushing, and push before relying on the new image in mkdox2.sh.
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Validation loop (executable, in order)
items.text:
# Level 1 — syntax/style
shellcheck mkdox2.sh docker/push_docker.sh
grep -c -- '--platform' mkdox2.sh                          # expect 0
head -1 docker/Dockerfile                                  # expect FROM zensical/zensical:0.0.74
# Level 2 — unit tests
./tests/run_tests.sh
# Level 3a — local single-arch image (before push)
(cd docker && docker buildx build --pull --platform linux/arm64 -t mkdox-zensical:test --load .)
docker run --rm --entrypoint zensical mkdox-zensical:test --version     # expect 0.0.74
tmp=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$tmp" && /Users/pforret/Code/mkdox/mkdox2/mkdox2.sh -D mkdox-zensical:test new demo && cd demo \
  && /Users/pforret/Code/mkdox/mkdox2/mkdox2.sh -D mkdox-zensical:test build && test -f site/index.html   # expect success, no platform warning
# serve (manual): ./mkdox2.sh -D mkdox-zensical:test serve, open the printed localhost URL, edit a page → hot-reload works
# Level 3b — push (after user confirms) and verify registry
bash docker/push_docker.sh
docker buildx imagetools inspect pforret/mkdox-zensical:0.0.74 | grep -E 'linux/(amd64|arm64)'   # expect both
docker buildx imagetools inspect pforret/mkdox-zensical:latest | grep -E 'linux/(amd64|arm64)'    # expect both
docker pull pforret/mkdox-zensical && docker run --rm --entrypoint zensical pforret/mkdox-zensical --version   # expect 0.0.74
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Steps
items.text:
• Read Zensical release notes 0.0.25–0.0.74: 0.0.33 switched the base to Alpine, 0.0.58 dropped x86/armv7 musl builds, 0.0.68 needs Python ≥3.11; none affect the CLI flags mkdox2 uses
  • Check the 0.0.74 base: Alpine, Python 3.14.4, /sbin/tini present, same ENTRYPOINT/CMD/WORKDIR
  • Pin FROM zensical/zensical:0.0.74 in docker/Dockerfile
  • Rewrite docker/push_docker.sh: cd to its own folder, read version from FROM, buildx --pull --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --push, tags :latest + :<version>
  • Drop --platform linux/amd64 from the 3 docker run calls in mkdox2.sh
  • Level 1: shellcheck push_docker.sh clean; mkdox2.sh has only the pre-existing SC2001 style notes (lines 639/641)
  • Level 2: ./tests/run_tests.sh, 2/2 ok
  • Level 3a: local arm64 build → zensical 0.0.74, all 5 plugins installed; mkdox2 new (simple, with_blog), mkdox2 serve (page served, hot-reload picks up edit, no platform warning), mkdox2 build (simple, with_blog, legacy mkdocs.yml project) all OK
  • Update CLAUDE.md Docker section and CHANGELOG.md
  • Level 3b: pushed (user confirmed); :latest and :0.0.74 both list linux/amd64 + linux/arm64 (same digest bb5cd59…); pulled image reports 0.0.74 on both arches; mkdox2 build with the default image OK
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Confidence
items.text: 9/10 that this can be implemented in one pass by an agent with only this file and the repo. Residual risk: a breaking change in Zensical 0.0.25–0.0.74 (CLI flags or a plugin failing on arm64) would need extra work.
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Tested with mkdox2 from this repo (./mkdox2 → mkdox2.sh); the mkdox2 on PATH is a basher clone at the old commit and mkdox is the older MkDocs-based tool (user). (recorded: decisions/2026-11-01.command-hints-and-help-text-in.md)
  • Deviation: also fixed the post-new hints in mkdox2.sh (lines 187/191) to use $script_prefix serve (= mkdox2 serve) instead of hardcoded mkdox serve, and the option help text "for mkdox new/build" → "mkdox2".
  • mkdox2 new prompts for a template when -B is missing; use -B simple in non-interactive tests. docker run -it needs a TTY (script -q /dev/null … when testing from a non-terminal).
  • Deviation: the PRP assumed buildx --push works on the default builder; it doesn't ("Multi-platform build is not supported for the docker driver"). push_docker.sh now creates/reuses a docker-container builder mkdox-builder. The local single-arch --load test still uses the default builder.
  • docs/index.md (regenerated usage text) and the docs/PRPs/zensical-migration.md deletion in the working tree are the user's own, unrelated to this item.
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

items.title: Deviations from the spec
items.text:
• push_docker.sh creates/reuses a docker-container buildx builder mkdox-builder: the PRP assumed buildx --push works on the default builder, but the default docker driver refuses multi-platform builds even when pushing. (recorded: decisions/2026-11-01.use-a-dedicated-docker-container-buildx.md)
  • Added scope: the hints after mkdox2 new (mkdox2.sh lines 187/191) now use $script_prefix serve (= mkdox2 serve) instead of hardcoded mkdox serve, and the option help text says "mkdox2 new/build"; mkdox is the older MkDocs-based tool (user).
  • Shellcheck criterion: mkdox2.sh is not fully clean at the default level because of 2 pre-existing SC2001 style notes, untouched by this item. (recorded: decisions/2026-11-01.leave-pre-existing-sc2001-shellcheck-notes.md)

items.title: Discoveries
items.text:
• Zensical 0.0.33 moved the official image to Alpine; 0.0.68 needs Python ≥3.11 (0.0.74 ships 3.14.4). /sbin/tini, ENTRYPOINT/CMD and WORKDIR /docs are unchanged, and all 5 pip plugins install on arm64.
  • docker run --platform linux/amd64 <image> re-tags the local :latest to the amd64 variant; afterwards plain runs on arm64 warn and get emulated until docker pull --platform linux/arm64.
  • The mkdox2 on PATH is a basher clone (~/.basher/cellar/packages/pforret/mkdox2) at the old commit; it keeps forcing amd64 until it's updated.
  • mkdox2 new blocks on the template prompt without -B, and docker run -it needs a TTY, so the repo has no non-interactive smoke test for new/build/serve (tests only check usage output).
  • Unrelated changes in the working tree, not from this item: deleted docs/PRPs/zensical-migration.md (user), regenerated docs/index.md usage, and a rebuilt site/ folder.
path: Update Zensical Docker image to latest version

path: Command hints and help text in mkdox2.sh say mkdox2, not mkdox

items.title: Context
items.text: While testing B1 (Zensical image update), the hint printed after mkdox2 new said "run 'mkdox serve'", and the option help said "for mkdox new/build". The user pointed out that mkdox is the older MkDocs-based tool and that the right command is mkdox2. The PRP didn't include this.
path: Command hints and help text in mkdox2.sh say mkdox2, not mkdox

items.title: Options considered
items.text:
• Leave as is (spec scope): users get pointed at the wrong, MkDocs-based tool.
  • Fix it in B1: small change, in the same file B1 already touched.
path: Command hints and help text in mkdox2.sh say mkdox2, not mkdox

items.title: Decision
items.text: Command hints and help text in mkdox2.sh say mkdox2, not mkdox
path: Command hints and help text in mkdox2.sh say mkdox2, not mkdox

items.title: Consequences
items.text: mkdox2.sh lines 187/191 use $script_prefix serve (resolves to mkdox2), and the help text says mkdox2. New user-facing hints should use $script_prefix, not a hardcoded name.

items.text: B1's acceptance criteria said shellcheck mkdox2.sh passes. It reports 2 SC2001 style notes (echo | sed 's/\r$//', lines 639/641) that were already there before B1.

items.title: Tag pforret/mkdox-zensical with :latest + the Zensical version
path: Tag pforret/mkdox-zensical with :latest + the Zensical version

items.title: Context
items.text: While planning the Zensical image update (0.0.24 → 0.0.74), the question was how docker/push_docker.sh should tag pforret/mkdox-zensical. Until now only :latest was pushed, although CLAUDE.md said the image shares the repo VERSION.md.
path: Tag pforret/mkdox-zensical with :latest + the Zensical version

items.title: Options considered
items.text:
• :latest + Zensical version (e.g. :0.0.74): the tag says what is inside the image and users can pin with -D pforret/mkdox-zensical:0.0.74; it doesn't say which mkdox release it goes with.
  • :latest + repo VERSION.md (e.g. :2.1.2): ties the image to a mkdox release, but bumping Zensical without bumping the repo would overwrite an existing tag.
  • Only :latest: simplest, but users can't pin and can't see the Zensical version.
path: Tag pforret/mkdox-zensical with :latest + the Zensical version

items.title: Decision
items.text: Tag pforret/mkdox-zensical with :latest + the Zensical version
path: Tag pforret/mkdox-zensical with :latest + the Zensical version

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Image tags follow Zensical releases, independently of the mkdox version. push_docker.sh reads the version from the FROM zensical/zensical:<x.y.z> line, so bumping Zensical is a one-line Dockerfile change. CLAUDE.md must no longer claim the image shares VERSION.md.
path: Tag pforret/mkdox-zensical with :latest + the Zensical version

items.title: Use a dedicated docker-container buildx builder (mkdox-builder) for the multi-arch push
path: Use a dedicated docker-container buildx builder (mkdox-builder) for the multi-arch push

items.title: Context
items.text: The PRP for B1 planned docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --push on the default builder. The first push failed: "Multi-platform build is not supported for the docker driver" (this Docker Desktop has no containerd image store).
path: Use a dedicated docker-container buildx builder (mkdox-builder) for the multi-arch push

items.title: Options considered
items.text:
• Default builder, as in the spec: doesn't work here.
  • Turn on the containerd image store in Docker Desktop: a machine-wide setting other people running push_docker.sh would also have to change.
  • A dedicated docker-container builder created by the script if missing: works without changing global settings; adds a buildkit container that stays around.
path: Use a dedicated docker-container buildx builder (mkdox-builder) for the multi-arch push

items.title: Decision
items.text: Use a dedicated docker-container buildx builder (mkdox-builder) for the multi-arch push
path: Use a dedicated docker-container buildx builder (mkdox-builder) for the multi-arch push

items.title: Consequences
items.text: docker/push_docker.sh runs docker buildx create --name mkdox-builder --driver docker-container on first use and builds with --builder mkdox-builder. Local single-arch --load test builds still use the default builder. Remove the builder with docker buildx rm mkdox-builder if needed.
path: Use a dedicated docker-container buildx builder (mkdox-builder) for the multi-arch push

items.title: Gotchas
items.text:
One line each, newest last. Start a line with path/to/file: and the session-start hook shows it when that file is in your diff.

  • 2026-11-01 docker/push_docker.sh: multi-arch buildx needs a docker-container builder; the default docker driver refuses even with --push (no containerd image store here)
  • 2026-11-01 mkdox2.sh: docker run --platform linux/amd64 <image> re-tags the local :latest to amd64; on arm64 later runs warn and run emulated until docker pull --platform linux/arm64 pforret/mkdox-zensical
  • 2026-11-01 docker/Dockerfile: zensical/zensical is Alpine-based since 0.0.33; use apk, not apt-get, for extra system packages

items.title: Zensical Compatibility with MkDocs Material
items.text: Summary of Zensical's compatibility status vs MkDocs Material for MkDocs, based on https://zensical.org/compatibility/.

items.title: Features
items.text:
All core MkDocs Material features are supported:

Category Status Core (install, build, serve, file layout, Jinja templates, YAML metadata) Supported Languages (60+), header, announcement bar, footer, social links, copyright Supported Git repo integration, code actions, tags, revisioning, 404 pages Supported Color palettes, light/dark toggle, custom colors/schemes, fonts, icons Supported Social cards, favicons, custom assets, template overrides Supported All 30+ Markdown extensions (admonitions, code blocks, Mermaid, math, etc.) Supported Blog, versioning, instant loading, search, analytics, SEO, offline usage Supported

Not yet available: Module system (planned replacement for hooks and plugins).

items.title: Template Overrides
items.text:
Zensical uses MiniJinja instead of Jinja2. Key differences:

  • No Python interpreter available — cannot call arbitrary Python functions
  • Templates must use available filters and tests only
  • Custom overrides based on Material for MkDocs 9.6.18+ should be compatible
  • A component system is on the roadmap to cover gaps

items.title: Plugin Compatibility
items.text:
Third-party MkDocs plugins are not loaded directly. Instead, Zensical replaces the most common ones with built-in functionality:

Plugin Zensical Status mkdocstrings Replaced by dedicated API documentation module (in development) git-revision-date-localized Native built-in git-authors Native built-in git-committers Native built-in macros Replaced by built-in component system minify Native minification + image compression mike Native versioning with improved workflows awesome-nav Native modular navigation literate-nav Native modular navigation static-i18n Native internationalization

Plugins not listed above (e.g. awesome-pages, blog, rss) are not yet supported in Zensical.

items.title: Zensical MiniJinja Template Reference
items.text: Zensical uses MiniJinja instead of Python's Jinja2. No Python interpreter is available — only the built-in filters and tests below.

items.title: Blog Index via MiniJinja — Feasibility
items.text:
Question: Can MiniJinja template overrides generate a docs/blog/index.md listing from posts in docs/blog/posts/?

Answer: No. MiniJinja cannot:

  • Read the filesystem — no way to scan a directory for .md files
  • Parse front matter — no YAML/string parsing beyond basic filters
  • Access other pages' content — the template context only has the current page, nav, and config

The nav object could theoretically be walked to find blog pages, but it lacks access to post metadata (date, excerpt, thumbnail) and there's no way to sort by date or extract content.

items.title: Workarounds
items.text:
Approach How Python hook (current) hooks/blog_context.py with on_page_markdown — scans posts, injects listing into blog/index.md at build time Build script Pre-generate blog/index.md as a build step before mkdox build Wait for Zensical blog Zensical lists blog as a supported feature; native blog support may arrive soon

The Python hook approach is the most practical solution until Zensical ships native blog support.
